technical_and_design_decisions: Treat each user story as a separately estimable work package, with discovery, implementation, testing, and documentation included where applicable.
Upgrade Reactor through the existing Maven dependency-management mechanism and resolve source or binary compatibility issues rather than introducing a parallel Reactor integration.
Implement multiple XD-Admin instances through Ambari-managed configuration and service definitions, using shared externalized state and avoiding node-local assumptions.

Implement @EnableModule as the module-level activation annotation and use @Input and @Output for channel discovery, with the framework creating channels and channel adapters through the application context.
Use reflection and Spring bean-definition registration for annotation processing, while preserving compatibility with explicitly declared channel beans where practical.
Complete Kryo work using the existing serialization architecture and benchmark representative payloads before selecting optimizations.
Move CI execution to EC2 using repeatable infrastructure and bootstrap scripts, retaining the existing CI test commands unless infrastructure incompatibilities require changes.
Treat module installation from Maven as a repository-resolution and runtime-installation workflow driven by a CLI artifactId, with repository credentials and repository URLs externalized.
Extract the serialization codec into Spring Integration as a reusable Maven artifact, then replace the Spring XD implementation with the dependency and preserve wire compatibility.
Implement the CloudController-based XD Admin SPI using the existing ModuleLauncher and Spring Cloud deployment abstractions, isolating Cloud Foundry-specific behavior behind the deployer interface.
Use unit tests for local behavior and focused integration or smoke tests for Ambari, EC2, Maven installation, serialization compatibility, and Cloud Foundry interactions.
Use the existing project build, test, and release conventions rather than introducing a new build system or deployment framework.
assumptions: The estimate covers one software increment across the eight listed user stories and includes coding, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and local validation.
The developer has access to the relevant Spring XD, Spring Integration, Spring Cloud, Ambari, Maven, AWS, and Cloud Foundry repositories and build environments.
Existing project architecture and test infrastructure are sufficiently functional; major unrelated defects and broad framework upgrades are out of scope.
Reactor 2.0.4 is compatible with the target Java and Spring XD baseline after limited source adaptation; a full Reactor API migration is not required.
Ambari supports configurable service counts or a manageable custom service configuration for multiple XD-Admin instances, and HA coordination infrastructure already exists or is unchanged.
The annotation-driven module model is intended for the existing module lifecycle and does not require a new module programming model, IDE tooling, or backward-incompatible public APIs.
Kryo optimization work is limited to the remaining identified optimizations, regression testing, benchmarking, and guideline documentation; no complete serialization redesign is included.
AWS account access, security permissions, and an existing CI provider or runner are available for the EC2 migration; procurement, networking approval, and 24-hour operations support are excluded.
The Maven module-installation story requires a working prototype or implementation of the CLI and runtime installation path, not a fully managed artifact marketplace or production repository service.
The serialization codec can be extracted without changing its externally observable serialization format, or compatibility tests can identify and address any required migration details.
Cloud Foundry access or a representative test environment is available, and the CloudController implementation is limited to the XD Admin SPI and ModuleLauncher integration described in the story.
Work-hour estimates represent focused engineering effort by one developer and exclude elapsed waiting time for external reviews, infrastructure provisioning, or third-party responses.

activities.activity_description: Inspect current Reactor usage, dependency graph, release compatibility, and expected source or binary changes; define the upgrade and validation plan.
Update Maven dependencies and dependency management, adapt affected code, resolve compilation and runtime compatibility issues, and update targeted tests.
Review current Ambari service definitions and determine the configuration, port, discovery, and shared-state changes required to run multiple XD-Admin instances.
Modify Ambari templates, service configuration, startup parameters, and instance handling so an installed XD cluster can start and manage multiple XD-Admin servers.

activities.activity_name: Test and document Ambari HA setup
activities.activity_description: Run installation and restart scenarios, verify concurrent XD-Admin instances and failure behavior, and document configuration and operational usage.
Define annotation semantics, channel naming and discovery rules, bean lifecycle behavior, backward compatibility, and error handling for @EnableModule, @Input, and @Output.
Add annotations, scanning and metadata processing, application-context registration, channel creation, channel adapters, validation, and integration with the existing module runtime.
Add unit and integration tests for input and output discovery, generated channels and adapters, invalid declarations, multiple channels, lifecycle behavior, and compatibility with explicit beans.
Provide usage examples, migration guidance, supported annotation combinations, naming rules, and troubleshooting information.
Review remaining optimization opportunities, implement serializer or registration changes, and remove avoidable allocation and reflection overhead within the existing design.
Create or update representative serialization benchmarks, verify correctness and compatibility, and investigate performance regressions.
Record configuration, registration, compatibility, performance, and usage guidelines for developers and operators.
Inventory current CI jobs and dependencies, select the EC2 execution model, and define instance, storage, credentials, networking, and retention requirements.
Create instance bootstrap and provisioning scripts, configure build dependencies and credentials, migrate CI jobs, and make test execution repeatable.
Run complete CI suites, troubleshoot environment-specific failures, verify cleanup and reproducibility, and document maintenance and recovery procedures.
Evaluate repository resolution, dependency isolation, artifact metadata, credentials, version selection, CLI syntax, and runtime installation alternatives.
Implement the selected artifactId-driven resolution and download path, integrate it with the running Spring XD runtime, and handle local repository and remote repository cases.
Test successful, missing, conflicting, authenticated, and invalid-artifact scenarios and document the CLI contract, repository configuration, and limitations.
Identify codec boundaries, public APIs, dependencies, package ownership, compatibility requirements, and the target Spring Integration module structure.

activities.activity_name: Move codec implementation into Spring Integration
activities.activity_description: Extract source and resources, update package and build metadata, establish the reusable Maven artifact, and adapt codec integration points.

activities.activity_name: Migrate XD and verify codec compatibility
activities.activity_description: Replace the XD-local implementation with the Spring Integration dependency, update configuration and tests, verify serialized data compatibility, and document the dependency transition.
Review the referenced Spring Cloud repositories and existing spike material, map XD Admin SPI and ModuleLauncher behavior to CloudController concepts, and define the deployment contract.
Implement the Cloud Foundry deployer and lifecycle operations, connect it to ModuleLauncher and XD Admin, handle environment and application metadata, and add required configuration.
Add unit and integration or smoke tests for deployment, update, status, stop, failure, and cleanup scenarios and verify pipeline-oriented module execution.
Document configuration, prerequisites, supported deployment operations, example pipeline usage, and known Cloud Foundry limitations.
Run the full build and regression suites across affected repositories, resolve cross-story dependency or packaging issues, and perform final compatibility verification.

activities.activity_name: Release preparation and final engineering documentation
activities.activity_description: Prepare release notes, dependency and migration notes, configuration samples, change summaries, and final build or packaging validation.
